summary: Weekly coaching 1-1 between sales coach Chris Klevan and closer Richard Claessen. Opens with roughly eleven minutes of personal conversation (Chris's bodybuilding and anabolic steroid history, gambling losses, bereavement, philosophy). Chris then reviews Richard's decision to end a call early after discovering the prospect had no money, and instructs him to run the full process regardless of qualification because the rep needs the practice and 'emotional closes'. The bulk of the call is a live role-play of the Objection C 'open wallet' money play, with Chris as closer and Richard as the prospect. Chris runs the full financial picture — monthly surplus, credit cards and limits, ETFs, crypto, credit score checked live on Credit Karma — then recommends third-party financing on a soft credit check, and handles the resulting spouse and fear objections. Closes with Chris self-critiquing that he should have isolated harder before the spouse objection surfaced.
notable: Stated coaching policy that reps should run the full sales process on prospects already known to be unable to pay: 'Right now, what's important for you, regardless of how the prospect shows up is actually just getting the rep of running... it's best to just run the call because the benefit for you is to just learn and get confident doing the process and emotionally close the person.'

Stated payment-plan policy: 'we don't really have any, like... Set payment plans. Everything we do is custom. just depends on what we can make work for the person.' Compare against the playbook Objection C line 'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up.'

Financing is the coached default for a hesitant buyer, not a last resort: 'let's just go ahead and do financing... the payments are probably going to be somewhere between like probably $500 to $600 a month to get you approved.' Chris characterises the application as 'a soft credit check, so it doesn't actually affect your credit score, and after 30 days it falls off.'
Coached price-framing: Richard said '$6,000 is quite a bit for some people' and was told 'Get that out of your head... Let that go' and to say 'To get to goal XYZ, it's just $6,000.'
Repeated social-proof claim used as the trust asset: 'we've worked with 1,200 clients' and 'if we were charging $6,000 across 1,200 people, that's a lot of money.'
Richard disclosed abandoning a live opportunity mid-pipeline to train: 'I can continue the call or I can actually go to the gym because otherwise I wasn't able to go. So I just went to the gym.'

Richard disclosed a prospect blocking his number after he used fit language: 'I told her, like, we only look for people who actually a fit with Trevor... she blocked my number.' Chris attributes it to funnel targeting: 'she probably looked at the funnel and saw that it was mainly targeting men who want to lose, like, 20 to 30 pounds, and she's a woman who wants to lose, like, 50 to 60 pounds.'
Recording disclosure was made on this internal call ('This meeting is being recorded'), which is more than appears on most of the sales calls in this batch.

The role-play contains a complete price presentation, objection sequence and financing close spoken as if to a real prospect. Anything scraping this corpus by content rather than by file classification will read it as a sales call.
